output.brief:
The Android drop is not caused by release 6.14 or by bots. On 3 March at 10:38 UTC, Corvane's automatic rule update added a rule (AUTO-LIB-17) that blocks requests from the nettle-http networking library on password-login paths. Our Android app uses that library, so real customers' password logins are being rejected with HTTP 403. About 92% of the blocked installs had logged in successfully before. Failures start within a minute of the rule going live, appear on every app version including older ones, and are absent from iOS and quick-unlock. Confidence is fairly high (about 85%) on the edge rule being the trigger; it is not yet confirmed by a test.

Next steps: ask Corvane, through the open ticket, to set AUTO-LIB-17 to log-only on the mobile password path, keeping rate limits and lockout, then confirm password success returns to about 97%. Do not raise bot sensitivity to high, and do not drop bot-blocked attempts from the KPI; both would make the lockout worse and hide it. Do not revert the password screen. Keep the 6.14 rollout under watch but it is not the cause. Contact-centre call growth is probably linked to the lockouts, but fee notices sent on 2 March make that unproven.
